title: Grid Teleportation Traversal
summary: Given a 2D character grid of size m x n, where each cell is either empty ('.'), an obstacle ('#'), or a portal (an uppercase letter 'A'-'Z'), start at the top-left cell (0, 0) and aim to reach the bottom-right cell (m - 1, n - 1).
statement: Given a 2D character grid of size m x n, where each cell is either empty ('.'), an obstacle ('#'), or a portal (an uppercase letter 'A'-'Z'), start at the top-left cell (0, 0) and aim to reach the bottom-right cell (m - 1, n - 1). You can move to adjacent cells (up, down, left, right) as long as the destination is not an obstacle. Stepping on a portal cell allows instant teleportation to any other cell with the same letter, but each portal can only be used once. Return the minimum number of moves required to reach the destination, or -1 if it is not possible.
constraints: matrix has at most 1,000 rows and columns; the start is not blocked.
Orthogonal movement costs one; teleporting between equal uppercase letters costs zero.
Each portal letter may be activated at most once; return -1 when the goal is unreachable.
hints: Grid moves have weight one and teleports weight zero, so shortest paths form a 0-1 BFS problem.
Index cells by portal letter; expand a letter once, putting zero-cost destinations at the deque front.
Pop a cell, expand and delete its portal group at the same distance, then enqueue unvisited walkable neighbors at distance+1.
The first expansion of a letter occurs at its minimum distance, so later expansions cannot improve any portal destination and the group is safely discarded.
editorial: The first expansion of a letter occurs at its minimum distance, so later expansions cannot improve any portal destination and the group is safely discarded.

tests.explanation: Teleport from the starting A to the center for free, then take two moves to the goal.
The only open route winds around the barriers and requires 13 moves.
